variants.title: Run the IO-aware loop
variants.context: FlashAttention changes execution order, not the attention rule. Bounded tiles are loaded on chip, a score tile is computed, running softmax statistics are merged, and the output is accumulated while the tile is discarded.
variants.prompt: A forward pass computes exact attention without materializing the full score matrix. Put the steps in order.

items.text: Compute a local score tile, since dense exact attention still visits the required query and key pairs.
Load bounded tiles of Q, K, and V from HBM into on-chip memory sized for the kernel and head dimension.
Accumulate the local probabilities against V into the output, then discard the score tile.
Merge softmax state by updating the running maximum and normalization sum, rescaling prior partial output.

variants.hint: One step is what lets independently processed blocks still produce one correct softmax.
variants.explanation: Tiling with online softmax statistics gives the same mathematical attention while the N by N surface is never written to HBM.

variants.title: Run the IO-aware loop
variants.context: FlashAttention changes execution order, not the attention rule. Bounded tiles are loaded on chip, a score tile is computed, running softmax statistics are merged, and the output is accumulated while the tile is discarded.
variants.prompt: A reviewer asks where the memory saving actually happens in the loop. Put the steps in order.

items.text: Update the running maximum and normalization sum so the discarded tile leaves its information behind.
Move one bounded tile of Q, K, and V on chip so the working set follows tile size, not sequence length.
Accumulate the output in HBM and drop the score tile instead of storing the full surface.
Compute the score tile for the block being processed and hold it only for that block.

variants.hint: Follow what is kept after each step, not what is computed.
variants.explanation: The saving comes from never writing the full score and probability surfaces, while the arithmetic stays quadratic in sequence length.

variants.title: Run the IO-aware loop
variants.context: FlashAttention changes execution order, not the attention rule. Bounded tiles are loaded on chip, a score tile is computed, running softmax statistics are merged, and the output is accumulated while the tile is discarded.
variants.prompt: The backward pass recomputes attention tiles instead of reading a stored probability matrix. Put its steps in order.

items.text: Rebuild the local probabilities from the saved softmax statistics rather than from stored values.
Load Q, K, V, and O tiles together with the saved normalization statistics from the forward pass.
Accumulate the gradients for that block and discard the recomputed tile.
Recompute the score tile for the block being differentiated.

variants.hint: Ask what the forward pass chose to save instead of the probability matrix.
variants.explanation: Recomputation trades arithmetic for reads, writes, and saved activation bytes, so its benefit depends on what the workload is limited by.

variants.title: Release the kernel change
variants.context: A kernel change ships like any other reversible release: freeze the version and shape contract, gate with dispatch, correctness and benchmark evidence, canary by workload, then keep a warm fallback and clean rollback.
variants.prompt: A team is enabling a fused attention path in a serving stack. Put the release steps in order.

items.text: Rollback cleanly: keep a compatible math or prior-kernel path warm with automatic stop conditions and a retained manifest.
Freeze the contract: pin framework, kernel package, compiler, driver, and container versions with the supported shape manifest.
Gate with evidence: run dispatch probes, output and gradient checks, target-shape benchmarks, and full-step memory tests.
Canary by workload: start with bounded traffic and watch fallbacks, rejections, OOMs, percentiles, and quality proxies.

variants.hint: One stage exists so that the numbers collected later describe a known configuration.
variants.explanation: Kernel support and dispatch rules are versioned dependencies, so the contract is pinned before any evidence is collected against it.

variants.title: Release the kernel change
variants.context: A kernel change ships like any other reversible release: freeze the version and shape contract, gate with dispatch, correctness and benchmark evidence, canary by workload, then keep a warm fallback and clean rollback.
variants.prompt: Traffic is moving to a new accelerator family next quarter. Put the steps in order for that migration.

items.text: Gate with evidence: rerun dispatch probes and correctness checks on the new hardware class, not only the old one.
Freeze the contract: pin the new driver, kernel package, and container versions and record the shapes they claim to support.
Canary by workload: expose bounded traffic on the new family while fallback counts and percentiles are watched.
Rollback cleanly: keep the previous path warm until the new family has cleared its own stop conditions.

variants.hint: Evidence collected on one hardware class does not transfer to another.
variants.explanation: A new device family reopens the whole release matrix, because eligibility, numerics, and performance are all device dependent.

variants.title: Release the kernel change
variants.context: A kernel change ships like any other reversible release: freeze the version and shape contract, gate with dispatch, correctness and benchmark evidence, canary by workload, then keep a warm fallback and clean rollback.
variants.prompt: During canary, rejection counts climb on long-context requests. Put the steps in order for the response.

items.text: Gate with evidence: reproduce the rejected shapes in the preproduction matrix instead of guessing from logs.
Rollback cleanly: return the affected traffic to the warm math path under the predeclared stop condition.
Canary by workload: hold or shrink exposure while the failing shape family is isolated.
Freeze the contract: confirm which package and shape manifest the canary was actually running.

variants.hint: Reproduce the failing shape before changing the production configuration.
variants.explanation: Telemetry names the shape family, the preproduction matrix reproduces it, and the warm fallback is what keeps the investigation from being an outage.

variants.title: Size the KV cache
variants.context: Tiled attention removes the N by N score surface, but the KV cache is a separate linear term. Its bytes are 2 for keys and values, times batch, times KV heads, times sequence length, times head dimension, times layers, times element bytes.
variants.prompt: A serving model uses 32 query heads but only 8 KV heads, head dimension 128, and 32 layers in BF16. For one sequence of 4096 tokens, how large is the KV cache?
variants.hint: Every term here is a power of two, so count the factors before multiplying.
variants.explanation: Two tensors times 1 batch times 8 KV heads times 4096 tokens times 128 dimensions times 32 layers times 2 bytes is 0.5 GiB, a linear term tiled attention does not remove.

mistakes.feedback: That counts keys only and forgets that values are cached too.
That uses the 32 query heads; grouped-query attention caches only the 8 KV heads.

variants.title: Size the KV cache
variants.context: Tiled attention removes the N by N score surface, but the KV cache is a separate linear term. Its bytes are 2 for keys and values, times batch, times KV heads, times sequence length, times head dimension, times layers, times element bytes.
variants.prompt: The same 8 KV head, 128 dimension, 32 layer BF16 model now serves 4 concurrent sequences of 4096 tokens each. How large is the KV cache in total?
variants.hint: Concurrency multiplies the cache the same way sequence length does.
variants.explanation: Two tensors times 4 batch times 8 KV heads times 4096 tokens times 128 dimensions times 32 layers times 2 bytes is 2 GiB, so concurrency is priced in cache bytes.

mistakes.feedback: That counts keys only and leaves out the value cache.
That prices a single sequence and ignores the four concurrent requests.

variants.title: Size the KV cache
variants.context: Tiled attention removes the N by N score surface, but the KV cache is a separate linear term. Its bytes are 2 for keys and values, times batch, times KV heads, times sequence length, times head dimension, times layers, times element bytes.
variants.prompt: A comparable model without grouped-query attention keeps all 32 KV heads, head dimension 128, and 32 layers in BF16. For 2 concurrent sequences of 4096 tokens, how large is the KV cache?
variants.hint: Compare which head count the cache is charged for.
variants.explanation: Two tensors times 2 batch times 32 KV heads times 4096 tokens times 128 dimensions times 32 layers times 2 bytes is 4 GiB, which is what grouped-query attention reduces.

mistakes.feedback: That counts keys only and omits the value tensor.
That charges 8 KV heads, but this model has no grouped-query reduction.

variants.title: Decide what may dispatch
variants.context: Kernel eligibility is a runtime decision from the actual inputs. Hardware family, dtype, head dimension, masking, dropout, pass direction, and package version all participate, and an API name never proves which kernel ran.
variants.prompt: A research model uses head dimension 320 on an A100 in BF16. The official CUDA package documents support up to head dimension 256. What is the defensible plan?
options: Force the fused backend anyway, since 320 is only slightly above a limit that is usually conservative.
Pad the head dimension to 512 so the tensors align, then dispatch to the fused kernel as usual.
Route these shapes to an exact fallback, measure that path, and do not report the result as FlashAttention.
optionFeedback: Documented limits are the support contract, and forcing an unsupported input produces an error rather than a faster kernel.
Padding past the documented maximum adds work and still leaves the shape outside the supported surface.
Correct: an unsupported head dimension is a dispatch gate, and silently benchmarking a fallback mislabels the result.
variants.hint: Head dimension is a gate, not a hint.
variants.explanation: Hardware generation is only one gate; dtype, head dimension, layout, masking, dropout, pass direction, and versions all decide eligibility.

variants.title: Decide what may dispatch
variants.context: Kernel eligibility is a runtime decision from the actual inputs. Hardware family, dtype, head dimension, masking, dropout, pass direction, and package version all participate, and an API name never proves which kernel ran.
variants.prompt: A service runs on T4 GPUs in FP16 and a developer installs the official CUDA FlashAttention-2 package, expecting a speedup. What should the team expect?
options: The package will select a slower Turing kernel automatically, so the only cost is a smaller improvement.
Turing is outside that package's target families, so a capability probe should log the outcome and route accordingly.
FP16 on any CUDA device satisfies the package contract, so the fused kernel will be selected for these shapes.
optionFeedback: Assuming a silent slower kernel invents behavior the package does not document.
Correct: the CUDA FlashAttention-2 path targets Ampere, Ada, and Hopper, and Turing is directed to a separate repository.
Dtype alone does not establish eligibility, since the hardware family is a separate gate.
variants.hint: Which gate does the device generation control?
variants.explanation: A capability probe at process start and in release tests is what turns an assumption about kernels into logged evidence.

variants.title: Decide what may dispatch
variants.context: Kernel eligibility is a runtime decision from the actual inputs. Hardware family, dtype, head dimension, masking, dropout, pass direction, and package version all participate, and an API name never proves which kernel ran.
variants.prompt: Enabling the fused path changes training loss in the last decimal places. A reviewer proposes requiring bitwise equality with the math backend before shipping. What is the right standard?
options: Compare only the final task metric, since small tensor differences cannot affect trained behavior.
Compare the candidate's error against the reference under tolerances reviewed per dtype and task.
Require bitwise equality, since exact attention should reproduce the reference result exactly.
optionFeedback: Task metrics alone can hide shape-specific outliers that output and gradient checks would catch.
Correct: exact means the same mathematical attention, and regrouped low-precision operations legitimately differ in the last bits.
Bitwise equality is not achievable when operations are reordered and accumulated differently.
variants.hint: What does exact mean in this lesson: identical bits, or the same rule?
variants.explanation: Numeric differences from reordering are expected, so correctness is judged against reviewed per-dtype tolerances across the release shape matrix.

variants.title: Map each part to its job
variants.context: An attention path has named parts: the tensors and their shapes, the gates that decide dispatch, and the correctness checks that each protect a different way a fused kernel can differ from the reference.
variants.prompt: Match each tensor to its shape and role in attention.

pairs.label: Queries
pairs.detail: Shape B by Hq by N by d, one row of scores per query position.

pairs.label: Keys and values
pairs.detail: Shape B by Hkv by N by d, with fewer KV heads under grouped-query attention.

pairs.label: Scores and probabilities
pairs.detail: Shape B by Hq by N by N when materialized, which is the quadratic activation pressure.

pairs.label: Output and row statistics
pairs.detail: Shape B by Hq by N by d plus the running maximum and normalization terms that merge blocks.

variants.hint: Two of these are quadratic in sequence length and two are not.
variants.explanation: Naming shapes first is what separates the quadratic surface a tiled kernel removes from the linear terms it does not.

variants.title: Map each part to its job
variants.context: An attention path has named parts: the tensors and their shapes, the gates that decide dispatch, and the correctness checks that each protect a different way a fused kernel can differ from the reference.
variants.prompt: Match each dispatch gate to what it constrains.

pairs.label: Hardware family
pairs.detail: Which architectures the kernel package targets, with other generations pointed elsewhere.

pairs.label: Dtype
pairs.detail: Whether the tensors are FP16 or BF16, since FP32 sits outside the CUDA package contract.

pairs.label: Head dimension
pairs.detail: Whether d is inside the documented maximum for the forward and backward paths.

pairs.label: Mask, dropout, and mode
pairs.detail: Whether causal or other masking, dropout, and the pass direction are covered for the shape.

variants.hint: Passing one gate says nothing about the others.
variants.explanation: Eligibility is the intersection of every gate, which is why a capability probe records the actual inputs rather than the API name.

variants.title: Map each part to its job
variants.context: An attention path has named parts: the tensors and their shapes, the gates that decide dispatch, and the correctness checks that each protect a different way a fused kernel can differ from the reference.
variants.prompt: Match each correctness check to the failure it is meant to catch.

pairs.label: Outputs and Q/K/V gradients
pairs.detail: A backward path that diverges while the forward result still looks acceptable.

pairs.label: Causal and non-causal runs
pairs.detail: Masking semantics that differ between the fused kernel and the reference.

pairs.label: All-masked rows and extreme logits
pairs.detail: Numerically degenerate inputs where the online softmax state can break down.

pairs.label: Model loss and critical slices
pairs.detail: A shape-specific error that one random tensor comparison would never surface.

variants.hint: Each check exists because one earlier check could pass while that failure hides.
variants.explanation: A release shape matrix with output, gradient, masking, boundary, and model-level checks is what supports a claim that the fused path is equivalent.
